rows.rationale: Aggro decks lack a storm/force-payoff combo gameplan, so this context is not applicable.
Aggro decks do not run Tron lands, so the Tron mana-advantage primitive is mechanically inapplicable.
Aggro decks don't run the Amulet of Vigor + bounce land + Titan engine, so this mana-advantage primitive is not applicable.
Aggro decks lack the cascade/Living-End shell structure this context targets, so the boost does not apply.
Cycling GY urgency is a cascade/combo-specific reanimation-timing primitive; aggro's clock doesn't hinge on graveyard state, so this context is N/A.
Living-End-shell gameplan boost is cascade/combo-specific and has no mechanical relevance to a pure aggro clock, so it stays at 0.0.
Free cycling (life-cost) preserves aggro's mana for pressure and enables an extra action per turn, slightly above the neutral default within the 1.5..2.5 band.
Aggro rarely runs cascade, so the free-spell clock contribution stays at the neutral baseline shared across archetypes.
Storm-count threshold for combo's force-payoff decision sits at the default 5.0, matching typical storm counts needed to justify going off.
Tron mana advantage is specific to Tron ramp decks; combo archetype has no mechanical tie to the Tron land package, so it is N/A.
Amulet+Titan bounce-land untap sequence generates roughly +4 mana, directly enabling combo-turn acceleration, matching the calibrated default.
Cascade-triggered free-spell chains in a Living-End-style combo shell are core to the gameplan, so the default cascade-specific boost of 8.0 applies without further inflation.
Combo (Living End-style) decks need low-GY urgency to enable early cascade/cycling reanimation, matching the default cascade/combo band.
Living-End-shell combo relies heavily on cycling-into-cascade reanimation as its core gameplan, warranting the upper-default boost.
Free cycling (pay-life) grants combo an extra selection/enabler action per turn cycle, slightly above neutral default within the 1.5-2.5 band.
Cascade's free-spell clock contribution is archetype-neutral (2.0-3.0); combo-specific cascade upside is already credited via cycling_cascade_boost/gameplan_boost, so no additional inflation here.

Control rarely runs cascade but the free-spell clock contribution is archetype-agnostic, so stay within the mandated 2.0-3.0 band near the low end.

Midrange cascade hits are a generic free-spell clock contribution, kept at the archetype-neutral default since cascade-specific incentives live in the dedicated cascade boost contexts.
